slot.brief: Show a substrate structure in a figure; ask which reagent (Lucas reagent sequence) distinguishes the given alcohols by rate/appearance.

stem: The alcohols shown are tested separately at room temperature. Which reagent and observation distinguish them by the onset of turbidity?
options: Concentrated $\text{HCl}$ and anhydrous $\text{ZnCl}_2$; butan-1-ol turns turbid first.
Concentrated $\text{HCl}$ and anhydrous $\text{ZnCl}_2$; butan-2-ol turns turbid within a few minutes, while butan-1-ol remains clear.
Dilute $\text{HCl}$ and anhydrous $\text{ZnCl}_2$; both turn turbid immediately.
Concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and anhydrous $\text{ZnCl}_2$; neither turns turbid.

verdicts.working: The upper structure is butan-2-ol (secondary); the lower is butan-1-ol (primary). With Lucas reagent (concentrated HCl and anhydrous ZnCl₂) at room temperature, the secondary alcohol turns turbid within a few minutes, while the primary alcohol remains clear.

working:
Lucas reagent: concentrated $\text{HCl}$ + anhydrous $\text{ZnCl}_2$.\nButan-2-ol is secondary: turbidity appears within a few minutes at room temperature.\nButan-1-ol is primary: no turbidity at room temperature.

Independent check: The upper structure is butan-2-ol (secondary); the lower is butan-1-ol (primary). With Lucas reagent (concentrated HCl and anhydrous ZnCl₂) at room temperature, the secondary alcohol turns turbid within a few minutes, while the primary alcohol remains clear.

figure.description: Draw two separate condensed structural formulae side by side. On the left, label butan-1-ol and draw CH3–CH2–CH2–CH2–OH. On the right, label butan-2-ol and draw CH3–CH(OH)–CH2–CH3. Show all bonds and the OH groups clearly.

draft.working: Lucas reagent: concentrated $\text{HCl}$ + anhydrous $\text{ZnCl}_2$.\nButan-2-ol is secondary: turbidity appears within a few minutes at room temperature.\nButan-1-ol is primary: no turbidity at room temperature.
draft.distractor_notes: A: reverses the relative reaction rates.\nC: uses dilute acid and incorrectly predicts immediate turbidity for both.\nD: substitutes sulfuric acid for the Lucas reagent and predicts no turbidity.
